assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Average acceleration
items.clue: Change in velocity divided by the time taken.

items.label: Deceleration
items.clue: A negative rate of change of velocity: slowing down.

items.label: Acceleration of free fall
items.clue: About 9.8 m/s^2 near the Earth's surface, whatever the mass.

items.label: Distance-time graph
items.clue: Its gradient gives the speed of an object moving along a straight line.

questions.stem: Two cars travel along the same straight road at 20 m/s, one heading north and the other heading south. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Their speeds are equal but their velocities differ
Their speeds and their velocities are both equal
Their speeds differ, but their velocities match
Neither their speeds nor velocities are equal

questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar, so both are 20 m/s. Velocity is speed in a given direction, and the directions are opposite, so the velocities differ.

questions.stem: What does the gradient of a distance-time graph tell you about the object?

options.text: The acceleration at that time
The distance moved so far
The total time of the trip
The speed at that moment

questions.explanation: The speed of an object can be calculated from the gradient of its distance-time graph: change in distance divided by change in time.

questions.stem: A motorbike speeds up from 5 m/s to 29 m/s in 6.0 s. What is its average acceleration?

options.text: 24 m/s

questions.explanation: Using a = (change in velocity) / t, the change in velocity is 29 - 5 = 24 m/s, so a = 24 / 6.0 = 4 m/s^2.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the velocity of a moving object?

options.text: Speed in a given direction
Simply another word for speed
How far it travels each second
How quickly its direction changes

questions.explanation: The velocity of an object is its speed in a given direction, which makes velocity a vector quantity.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph a straight line passes through the origin and through the point (8.0 s, 120 m). What is the speed of the object?

options.text: 15 m/s
8 m/s

questions.explanation: The gradient is the change in distance divided by the change in time: 120 m / 8.0 s = 15 m/s.

questions.stem: A train slows down uniformly from 30 m/s to 10 m/s in 40 s. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is now travelling backwards along the track at 10 m/s
It is decelerating, and so its acceleration is -0.5 m/s^2
It is decelerating at 0.25 m/s^2, from 10 m/s in 40 s
It is accelerating at 0.5 m/s^2 along the track

questions.explanation: An object that slows down is decelerating. The change in velocity is -20 m/s in 40 s, so the acceleration is -0.5 m/s^2.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly classifies distance, displacement, speed and velocity?

options.text: Distance and displacement are scalars, with the others vectors
Distance and speed are scalars; displacement and velocity are vectors
Distance and velocity are scalars, displacement and speed vectors
All four are vectors, since each one has a size and a unit

questions.explanation: Distance and speed carry no direction, so they are scalars; displacement and velocity each include a direction, so they are vectors.

questions.stem: Part of a distance-time graph for a car is a horizontal straight line. What is the car doing during that part?

options.text: It is moving at a steady speed there
It is stationary and staying put
It is going back towards the start
It is speeding up all the time

questions.explanation: A horizontal line has zero gradient, so the distance is not changing and the speed is zero.

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of the acceleration of a family car pulling away from traffic lights?

options.text: About 100 m/s^2, so reaching 12 m/s in around 0.1 s
About 9.8 m/s^2, the same as an object falling
About 2 m/s^2, reaching some 12 m/s in about 6 s
About 0.02 m/s^2, reaching 12 m/s in 10 min

questions.explanation: A sensible everyday estimate: 2 m/s^2 sustained for 6 s gives 12 m/s, a reasonable town speed.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph the line curves upwards and becomes steeper as time goes on. What does this show?

options.text: The object is slowing down as time goes on
The object moves at a steady high speed
The object is moving away from the start
The object is speeding up as time goes on

questions.explanation: An increasing gradient means the distance covered each second is growing, so the object is speeding up.

questions.stem: What does the gradient of a velocity-time graph give?

options.text: The distance it has travelled
The speed it has at that moment
The average velocity so far
The object's acceleration

questions.explanation: The acceleration of an object can be calculated from the gradient of a velocity-time graph.

questions.stem: A car accelerates uniformly at 3.5 m/s^2 from an initial velocity of 24 m/s over a distance of 7.0 m. What is its final velocity?

options.text: 25 m/s
7 m/s

questions.stem: A car is driven round a roundabout at a steady 8 m/s. Which statement about its motion is correct?

options.text: Both its speed and its velocity stay constant all round
Its velocity is constant but its speed is changing
Its speed is constant but its velocity keeps changing
Neither its speed nor its velocity is constant

questions.explanation: Motion in a circle involves constant speed but changing velocity, because the direction of motion changes continuously.

questions.stem: The distance-time graph for an accelerating car is a curve. How should the speed of the car at 6 s be found?

options.text: Join the origin to the point at 6 s and find that gradient
Read the distance at 6 s straight off the vertical axis
Draw a tangent to the curve at 6 s and measure its gradient
Find the area under the curve up to the 6 s point

questions.explanation: For an accelerating object the speed at a particular time is the gradient of the tangent drawn to the distance-time graph at that time.

questions.stem: A velocity-time graph for a cyclist is a straight line rising from 0 m/s to 15 m/s over 8.0 s. What distance does the cyclist travel in that time?
questions.explanation: The distance is the area under the line, a triangle: 0.5 × 8.0 s × 15 m/s = 60 m.
